text.p: Gold, boosted by a dramatic surge in silver, consolidated a bounce from 40-month lows on Friday afternoon in a bullion market where the mood was noticeably brighter than of late.
Gold had been under intense pressure lately, falling below $350 an ounce this week from above $410 a year ago, on a specualtor bale out and fears that central banks may sell gold from their reserves.

Silver held centre stage in early Friday trading in London when it extended a rally sparked on Thursday by U.S. investment funds. Silver's midday fixing at 497.25 cents was a three-month high and up nearly 25 cents from Thursday's fix.
"It was wild, and it was all silver," a dealer said. "A lot of people believe this is the start of a major recovery for both gold and silver."
Silver eventually eased back from the highs, but at $4.92/$4.94 it was still four cents up from Thursday's strong London close.
Gold followed silver higher in after U.S. investment funds decided there was a play in the gold-silver ratio and began to buy silver on Thursday.
Prices eased in the afternoon to fix at $352.50 an ounce, down from $352.95 in the morning. Still, gold was still well above Thursday's 40-month low fix of $348.00.
But the jury was still out on gold's recovery prospects, with a number of analysts and dealers cautious that the gains were short term.
Producer selling could be expected, especially from South African and North American producers which the market perceived to be under hedged, dealers said.
"Gold has not recovered out of its downside channel," an analyst said. The same was true for silver, which needed to notch up several constructive closes to build confidence.
"Silver looks very dangerous, very volatile," a dealer said.
Silver's rise was attributed to its resiliance while gold was being sold down in recent weeks, which courted confidence in the white metal as an investment.
"The complex, through silver, was supported by a major U.S. fund on Thursday," a senior market analyst said.

"There was growing confidence that the white metals had been drawn down by the weight of selling in gold and not with economic justification and that they would not follow gold to the same extent," he added.
Platinum was $1.50 ahead at $357.75/$358.75 having recovered from a 40-month low fix on Thursday of $355.85.
